newsitem.title: FRANCE: No trains in Channel Tunnel until Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: No trains in Channel Tunnel until Wednesday.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel said trains may start running again on Wednesday, abandoning hopes of resuming traffic on Tuesday night after a fire aboard a truck shuttle damaged the tunnel.

"There will not be any trains tonight or overnight. We hope to be able to start again tomorrow morning (Wednesday) but we don't know at what time," a spokeswoman for Anglo-French operator Eurotunnel SA Plc told Reuters.
Eurotunnel, which had earlier said it hoped partial traffic could resume on Tuesday night, said traffic would start with Eurostar high-speed passenger trains, with goods trains running later.
The French state rail company SNCF said it was not sure when the tunnel would reopen. It urged Eurostar passengers with bookings for Wednesday to postpone their trip.
Passengers who turn up would be put on ferries or would get their money back.

About 70 French and British fire-fighters fought all night against the blaze which started on Monday night 18 kms (11 miles) from the French entrance. Fire damaged the tunnel over about 600 metres (yards) and French Transport Minister Bernard Pons told parliament repairs would take several weeks.
